messages:
alex: Quick question — we need to pick an epoch alignment approach for ingest/billing windows. Fixed wall-clock epochs (hourly aligned) vs event-time windows with watermarking. Thoughts?

maria: My gut is event-time with watermarking for accuracy, but it complicates billing cutover and SLA guarantees.

pk: +1 for event-time for correctness. But we need a practical policy for late tokens — how far do we accept them before we finalize?

kevin: If we allow long tails we blow up reconciliation. For billing I prefer bounded lateness + explicit late-credit path. Eg accept late events for 10m, after that route to "late_adjustments" ledger.

jen: Can we separate attribution resolution from billing finalization? Resolve attribution event-time, but cut billing windows on fixed epochs with a deterministic merge step. That gives operational cutover predictability.

alex: @jen that's interesting — so event-time attribution (best-effort) + deterministic compaction at epoch boundary. What about audits and backfills?

maria: Audits need full provenance. Whatever we do, keep raw events immutable for at least 90 days and keep an index to map event->finalized attribution. Backfill path should be able to re-run compaction without changing primary ledger ids.

pk: Implementation sketch: ingestion attaches event_time, ingest_ts, fingerprint. We write to raw topic. A streaming job emits provisional credits keyed by attribution_hash. We keep a reconciliation topic for corrections. At epoch boundary a finalize job consumes provisional + corrections -> append-only finalized ledger.

kevin: Edgecases: chunked requests spanning epochs. We need deterministic assignment rules (first token epoch vs last token epoch vs attribution vector split). We should prefer attributing to request start epoch for stability. Document it clearly.

jen: Also tombstones for deletes. If customer requests data deletion, we must emit tombstones that invalidate provenance and trigger recompute of affected epoch's aggregated credits. That recompute should land in the reconciliation topic, not rewrite finalized rows.

alex: OK, tradeoffs summary: fixed epochs = simple finalization, easier SLAs; event-time attribution = accuracy but needs bounded lateness and late-adjustment path. Proposal: event-time attribution with 10m watermark, finalize on wall-clock epoch every hour with a deterministic compaction pass that consumes reconciliations. Deletions funnel through reconciliation pipeline.

maria: +1 on 10m as starting point. We can monitor late-arrival rate and bump if needed. Add metrics: percent late by tenant, recredit volume, finalization latency.

pk: Operational notes: add a metric for "finalize_rewrites" count and a pager if reconciled credits exceed X% of epoch volume. Also set cold-path backfill runbook (batch re-run) for >30d windows.

metering-bot: Deploy note: next canary for the finalize job scheduled Thu 03:00 UTC. Release playbook: canary -> monitor finalize_rewrites -> promote.

kevin: One more: data retention for raw events must be long enough to support audits and backfills. We should require 90d for raw topic, 365d for audit attachments (compressed snapshots).

jen: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with diagrams: ingest -> provisional stream -> reconciliation topic -> hourly finalizer -> finalized ledger + audit index. Include examples for chunked requests and delete flow.

alex: Thanks everyone. @maria can you own the metrics dashboard? @pk can you sketch the finalize job idempotency and compaction algorithm? I'll consolidate into the RFC. :thumbsup:

maria: Yep, will do.

pk: On it. I'll post a short pseudo-code thread later.

alex: Closing for now. If anyone spots a hard failure mode (esp around deletions) throw it here.
